disciplines.title: Prepare and emergency response
disciplines.question: Does this problem need an 8D, and what protects the customer right now, before anyone knows the cause?

disciplines.title: Establish the team
disciplines.question: Who knows the product and the process, who leads the team, and who as champion removes the obstacles?

disciplines.title: Describe the problem
disciplines.question: What is wrong with what, in numbers? Answer 5W2H, set IS against IS NOT, then write one problem statement. No causes yet.

disciplines.title: Interim containment actions
disciplines.question: How do you stop the next bad delivery while the cause is still unknown? Sort every place the suspect stock can be, and prove that the containment works.

disciplines.title: Root cause and escape point
disciplines.question: Why did it happen, and why did nobody catch it? Two root causes, each verified: you can turn the problem on and off with it.

disciplines.title: Permanent corrective actions
disciplines.question: Which actions remove both root causes? Choose them, and verify that they work before you implement them.

disciplines.title: Implement and validate
disciplines.question: Put the actions in place, show with data that the problem is gone, and only then remove the containment.

disciplines.title: Prevent recurrence
disciplines.question: Which systems change so that this cannot happen again, here or anywhere similar?

disciplines.title: Recognise the team and close
disciplines.question: Thank the team for what it did, write down what you learned, and close the report.

criteria: The symptom is defined and measured.
The customer who saw it and the parties affected are known.
The numbers show a gap, or its severity, urgency or growth makes it a priority.
Management commits the people and the time to fix it at the root and prevent it from coming back.
It is too complex for one person to solve alone.

w2h.label: What is the problem?
w2h.placeholder: The defect on the object, in plain words: which item, which fault.

w2h.label: Why is it a problem?
w2h.placeholder: What it costs or breaks for the customer: shelf gaps, fees, a missed service level.

w2h.label: Where was it seen?
w2h.placeholder: Route, customer site, line, zone, location on the item.

w2h.label: When was it seen?
w2h.placeholder: Since when, on which shifts or days, in which phase (receipt, pick, delivery).

w2h.label: Who found it, who is affected?
w2h.placeholder: Who detected it and who is affected. Roles, not blame.

w2h.label: How was it found, how does it show?
w2h.placeholder: How it was detected and how the fault appears in the process.

w2h.label: How many?
w2h.placeholder: The count and the base: 144 of 4,800 lines, the trend, other areas for comparison.

isNot.label: What
isNot.isNot: Similar objects or defects that could be affected but are not

isNot.label: Where
isNot.isNot: Where it could be, but is not

isNot.label: When
isNot.is: When it first appeared, when it shows
isNot.isNot: When it could show, but does not

isNot.label: Extent
isNot.is: How many, how big, the trend
isNot.isNot: How many could be affected, but are not

preventions.name: Update the FMEA
preventions.hint: Add the failure mode and its cause, then re-rate occurrence and detection.

preventions.name: Update the control plan
preventions.hint: The new check: what, how often, by whom, and what to do when it fails.

preventions.name: Update standard work
preventions.hint: Change the instruction at the workplace, so the new way is the only way.

preventions.name: Train the people
preventions.hint: Everyone who does the work, on every shift, with a sign-off.

preventions.name: Read across to similar products and processes
preventions.hint: Where else can the same cause sit: other sites, lines, zones, products?

preventions.name: Other system change
preventions.hint: A policy, a supplier agreement, a design rule.

fields.title: e.g. Wrong items to the retailer on route R7
fields.eraText: e.g. No roll cage of the route leaves without a check; the customer is called today.
fields.statement: One or two sentences: what is wrong with what, where, since when and how many. No cause, no blame.
fields.containment: e.g. 100 % scan of every roll cage of the route before loading
fields.verification: e.g. 0 wrong lines in the customer's receipt audit since
fields.cleanMark: e.g. Green dot on the label of every checked roll cage
fields.occurrence: Why did it happen? The cause in the process that, when present, makes the problem appear.
fields.escapePoint: e.g. Pick confirmation, then the dispatch check
fields.escape: Why was it not detected? The control that should have caught it, and why it did not.
fields.verifyHow: How it was turned on and off: a trial, a test, the data before and after.
fields.notes: Your chain of whys or the likely causes of a fishbone; they can be taken from 5 Whys and Fishbone below.
fields.pca: A change to the process that removes the cause, not a reminder.
fields.pcaCheck: e.g. Trial pick: 0 wrong in 400 picks
fields.implementation: e.g. EAN scan live in zone C on all shifts
fields.period: e.g. Two weeks after the change
fields.result: What the data shows after the change, and since when.
fields.recognition: Who did what; how the team was thanked.
fields.lessons: What you would do the same and what differently next time.
fields.closedBy: e.g. Champion or the customer's quality contact

tips: D3 protects the customer within a day. Sort every place the suspect stock can be: in the warehouse, on the road, at the customer.
D2 is 5W2H and IS / IS NOT. The difference between where it is and where it is not points to the cause; a guess does not.
Why it happened, and why nobody caught it. A cause is verified when you can turn the problem on and off with it.
D5 proves an action works in a trial; D6 proves with the data that the problem is gone. Remove the containment only after that.
Close the system, not just the case.
D7 changes the FMEA, the control plan, the standard work and the training, and looks for the same cause elsewhere.

example.title: Wrong items to the retailer on route R7
example.customer: Retail customer, 12 stores in the north region

d0.era: No roll cage of route R7 leaves the dock unchecked from the next loading on. The account manager calls the retailer the same morning and agrees a swap run for the wrong lines.

w.what: Stores receive a wrong variant of the ordered item: another size or flavour of the same product line, e.g. 1 L instead of 0.5 L of the same drink.
w.why: The ordered item is missing on the shelf and another is in surplus. The retailer charges €15 per wrong line (€2,160 in five days) and the agreed 99.5 % correct lines is broken.
w.where: Route R7, the retailer's 12 stores in the north region. The lines are picked in zone C of the DC.
w.when: Since the re-slotting of zone C, one week before the complaint, on both shifts. Found in the retailer's goods-receipt audit.
w.who: Found by the store teams and the retailer's receipt audit; the complaint reached our account manager.
w.how: The picker confirms the location's check digit and takes the look-alike from the next slot. The dispatch check counts roll cages and store labels, not items.
w.howMany: 144 of 4,800 lines (3.0 %) in five delivery days on R7; the other routes 0.2 % (42 of 21,000).

what.is: A wrong variant of the ordered item (other size or flavour, same product line)
what.isNot: Missing lines, damaged goods, wrong quantities, items of another product line
what.diff: Look-alike variants with the same label colour

where.is: Route R7, 12 stores; lines picked in zone C
where.isNot: The other routes (0.2 %); zones A, B and D
where.diff: Only R7's stores order both variants (regional range); zone C was re-slotted

when.is: Since the re-slotting of zone C, on both shifts
when.diff: The re-slotting put look-alike variants in adjacent slots

extent.is: 144 of 4,800 lines (3.0 %), steady from day to day; 9 look-alike pairs
extent.isNot: Not growing; not the other SKUs of zone C
extent.diff: The 9 pairs sit side by side since the re-slotting

d2.statement: Since the re-slotting of zone C, 3.0 % of the order lines delivered on route R7 to the retailer's 12 stores are a wrong variant of the ordered item (144 of 4,800 lines in five delivery days), against 0.2 % on the other routes.

actions.text: 100 % item scan of every R7 roll cage at dispatch before loading; wrong lines corrected on the spot
actions.verified: 84 wrong lines corrected in the first three days; a re-check of 200 scanned lines found none

actions.text: Check the two R7 trucks already on the road at store arrival and swap the wrong lines
actions.verified: All 31 swapped the same day; the store teams confirmed by mail

actions.text: Recount with the stores the deliveries of the last five days; swap run for the wrong lines
actions.verified: 144 lines swapped in one run; the retailer's credit note matches the 144

d3.cleanMark: Green dot on the label of every scanned roll cage; the retailer's receipt audit found 0 wrong lines on R7 since the first green-dot delivery.

occurrence.text: The re-slotting of zone C put look-alike variants of the same article (same label colour, sizes 0.5 L and 1 L) in adjacent slots: 9 pairs. Only the R7 stores order both variants, so only R7 lines are exposed.
occurrence.how: Turned on and off in a trial pick: 400 picks from the adjacent look-alike slots, 11 wrong (2.75 %); the same 400 picks with the variants three slots apart, 0 wrong.

escape.point: Pick confirmation in zone C, then the dispatch check
escape.text: A pick is confirmed with the location's check digit only, not the item barcode; the dispatch check counts roll cages and labels, not items. A wrong variant from the right location passes both.
escape.how: In the trial all 11 wrong picks passed the check digit and the dispatch check; with an item (EAN) scan at the pick, all 11 were stopped.

d4.notes: Fishbone with the late shift: Method (no slotting rule for look-alikes), Material (same label colour), Measurement (check digit, not the item). 5 Whys: wrong variant, because next slot, because re-slotting by sales speed only, because no look-alike rule.

actions.text: Re-slot zone C: look-alike variants at least three slots apart and on different levels; the rule added to the WMS slotting check
Confirm every pick in zone C with an item (EAN) scan instead of the location check digit
actions.verification: Trial: 11 of 11 wrong picks stopped; pick rate −2 %, accepted

actions.text: Zone C re-slotted, the 9 look-alike pairs apart
EAN scan at the pick live in zone C on all shifts
Stop the 100 % dispatch scan of R7 after two clean weeks

d6.period: Two weeks after the EAN scan went live, measured at the dispatch scan
d6.result: Wrong lines on R7 down from 3.0 % to 0.09 % (9 of 9,600), below the 0.2 % of the other routes. The retailer's receipt audit found none.

lines.text: Process FMEA, picking: failure mode "look-alike variant in the adjacent slot" added; occurrence and detection re-rated after the EAN scan
Control plan: weekly slotting check for look-alike pairs; EAN scan rate as a daily KPI with a reaction plan
Standard work for every slotting change: look-alike check before the change is released
All zone C pickers and the slotting team briefed on look-alikes and the scan rule, both shifts, signed
Read-across: check zones A, B and D and the second DC for look-alike pairs side by side
